documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Episode 11/03/2021 – 01/12/2022, twice weekly; two visits cancelled.

Diagnosis: right superior gluteal nerve palsy.
Progress: right hip abduction strength 3+/5 at evaluation, 4/5 at discharge. Single-leg stance on the right longer and steadier, still with mild pelvic drop. Patient reports the hip gives way on stairs much less often. Mild limp persists, more when tired.
Discharged to independent home exercise program (side-lying abduction, clamshells, bridges, single-leg balance). Re-referral welcome if she plateaus or regresses.

Exam: mild R Trendelenburg limp. Paraspinal tenderness. Line site fine.
A/P: R superior gluteal nerve palsy — improving with PT, keep up home exercises. TPN — CMP, Mg today. LBP — chronic, stable. MDD/GAD — per psych. Colonoscopy with GI in March. RTC after that.

documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY — 03/22/2022
Indication: colorectal cancer screening, history of Crohn's disease (small bowel), short bowel syndrome.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: adequate.
Findings: The colon was examined in full. Colonic mucosa normal throughout. No polyps. No ulceration, erythema or other signs of active inflammation. Normal retroflexion in the rectum.
Impression: Normal colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 5 years. Continue vedolizumab and TPN as directed.
Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

documents.body:
Video visit (pt at home, consents to telehealth).
Colonoscopy 3/22 normal, repeat 5 yr. Mood "pretty steady," seeing psych every 3 months. Sleep so-so, still uses diphenhydramine. Alprazolam about once a week now. Back pain "same as always" — doing the PT home exercises most days, which she thinks helps the hip more than the back. No seizures. Not smoking.
Appears well on video, bright, conversational.
Plan: no changes. Physical in July (Pap due). Call sooner prn.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, 47F.

Since last year: PT for R superior gluteal nerve palsy (Nov–Jan), better. Colonoscopy 3/2022 normal. No seizures since 12/2020. No hospital visits. GI review last fall, TPN unchanged. Psych q3 months — sertraline/bupropion unchanged.
Current: mood steady, some bad weeks. Back pain chronic. Hip occasionally weak on stairs. Not smoking (quit 2/2021). Weekend cocktail or two.

Meds: sertraline 100 daily; bupropion XL 150 daily; alprazolam 0.25 prn; diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn; lamotrigine 100 bid; norethindrone/EE 1/20 daily; MVI; TPN nightly; vedolizumab q8wk (GI).
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance, ineffective); gabapentin (ineffective).

Exam: NAD. Weight 59.8. HEENT nl. Neck supple, no LAD, thyroid nl. CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs CTA. Abd soft, NT, healed scars. Line exit site clean. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal, Pap/HPV collected. Ext no edema. Gait with slight R hip drop. Mood euthymic-ish, affect full.
PHQ-9 10, GAD-7 8, AUDIT-C 2.

Plan:
1. Pap with HPV today.
2. Mammo — ordered for December.
3. PCV20 today; she smoked for years and is on long-term TPN through a central line. Discussed and agreed.
4. Labs: CBC, CMP, Mg, B12, D, iron studies.
5. Colonoscopy UTD (2022), next 2027 per GI.
6. Flu/COVID this fall.
7. Mood/anxiety — stable on current regimen per psych.

documents.title: Physical results and Pap
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tracy — everything from your physical is normal. Your Pap was normal and the HPV test negative, so you won't need another one for five years. Blood counts, kidney/liver tests, magnesium, B12, vitamin D and iron are all fine.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD — regional hospital
Arrival 11/04/2022 07:50

CC: RUQ pain

HPI: 47-year-old woman with small bowel Crohn's disease and short bowel syndrome on home TPN via tunneled catheter, here with a full day of steady, severe pain under the right ribs that bores through to her back. Nauseated, felt feverish overnight. Bowel pattern unchanged from her baseline, no urinary complaints.

PMH: Crohn's, short bowel/TPN, recurrent MDD, GAD, chronic LBP, temporal lobe epilepsy, R superior gluteal nerve palsy.
Meds: sertraline, bupropion XL, alprazolam prn, diphenhydramine prn, lamotrigine, OCP, multivitamin, TPN, vedolizumab IV q8 weeks.
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance/ineffective), gabapentin (ineffective).
SH: former light smoker, social alcohol, on disability.

Triage: T 38.2 °C (100.8 °F), HR 102, BP 135/85.
Exam: uncomfortable. Abdomen: tender in the right upper quadrant with inspiratory arrest on palpation (Murphy sign positive). No peritoneal signs elsewhere. Line site clean.

Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250. T bili 1.8, alk phos 120, AST 50, ALT 45. Amylase 90, lipase 85.
RUQ US: thickened GB wall, pericholecystic fluid, no stones.

MDM: Acute acalculous cholecystitis in a long-term TPN patient. Blood cultures drawn, IV piperacillin-tazobactam started, IV fluids; pain and nausea treated. General surgery consulted — will admit for cholecystectomy.

Disposition: admitted to surgery.

reports.text: Specimen: gallbladder, laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Gross: intact gallbladder with edematous, thickened wall; no calculi identified. Microscopic: transmural acute inflammation with mucosal ulceration and wall edema. No dysplasia or malignancy. Cystic duct margin unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Acute cholecystitis, acalculous. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

medications.sig: Take 1-2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for incision pain

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — General Surgery, regional hospital
Admitted 11/04/2022 — Discharged 11/07/2022

Diagnosis: acute acalculous cholecystitis.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 11/05/2022 (four ports, uncomplicated, EBL minimal).

Course: Admitted from the ED with RUQ pain, fever and leukocytosis; ultrasound showed a thick-walled gallbladder with pericholecystic fluid and no stones. Treated with IV piperacillin-tazobactam and taken to the OR the next morning. Postoperatively she tolerated sips and resumed her usual nightly TPN on POD 0 with home infusion's formula. Afebrile from POD 1; pain well controlled. Blood cultures no growth. Pathology: acute cholecystitis, acalculous, no dysplasia.

Discharge medications: resume all home medications (sertraline 100 mg daily, bupropion XL 150 mg daily, alprazolam 0.25 mg prn, diphenhydramine 25 mg qhs prn, lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, norethindrone/EE daily, multivitamin, TPN nightly; vedolizumab on her usual schedule with GI). No antibiotics needed after discharge. Acetaminophen as needed for incision pain; no NSAIDs (intolerance).
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Follow-up: PCP within 1–2 weeks; surgery clinic 2 weeks for port-site check. Call for fever, worsening pain, redness at the incisions, or jaundice.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Admitted 11/4–11/7 with acute acalculous cholecystitis, lap chole 11/5 (path acute cholecystitis, no stones). Discharge summary and ED record reviewed; med list reconciled — no changes.
Doing well. Incision soreness only, using acetaminophen once or twice a day. Eating her usual small amounts, TPN nightly. No fever, no jaundice. Surgery clinic f/u next week.
Exam: afebrile. Weight 59.4 (59.8 in July). Four port sites healing, clean and dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the umbilical port. Line site clean.
A/P: s/p lap chole for acalculous cholecystitis — recovering well. Repeat LFTs and CBC today. Cholecystitis resolved. Weight essentially stable; GI aware via discharge summary.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, pulmonary embolism protocol. Filling defects in segmental pulmonary arterial branches of the right lower lobe, consistent with acute pulmonary emboli. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries patent. Right ventricle not enlarged; RV/LV ratio normal; no septal flattening. Lungs clear without consolidation, infarct or effusion. Right-sided tunneled central venous catheter with tip at the cavoatrial junction. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Acute segmental pulmonary emboli in the right lower lobe. No CT evidence of right heart strain.

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
Date of service 10/29/2023

Chief complaint: short of breath

48-year-old woman with Crohn's disease, short bowel syndrome on nightly TPN via a tunneled catheter, brought in by her partner after shortness of breath came on suddenly this afternoon. Five days ago she had a right knee arthroscopy at an outside surgery center and has been mostly on the couch since, getting around very little.

Meds: sertraline 100 mg, bupropion XL 150 mg, alprazolam 0.25 mg prn, diphenhydramine 25 mg qhs prn, lamotrigine 100 mg bid, combined OCP, TPN nightly, vedolizumab IV q8 weeks.
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin (both intolerance/ineffective).
SH: smokes about a pack of cigarettes a week. A cocktail now and then on weekends.
FH: maternal aunt with DVT.

Vitals: BP 125/85, HR 110.
Exam: anxious, speaking full sentences. Tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Right knee with arthroscopy portals clean, dressing intact. Calves soft. Line site clean.

Workup: CBC, BMP unremarkable. CTA chest: acute segmental emboli in the right lower lobe, no right heart strain.

Impression: acute pulmonary embolism, provoked (post-operative, reduced mobility; on estrogen-containing OCP, smoker).
Plan: enoxaparin 1 mg/kg (60 mg) SC now and q12h — chosen over an oral agent given her short bowel. Stop the combined OCP. Observation admission for monitoring.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Hospital Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Hospital Medicine, regional hospital
Observation 10/29/2023 – 10/31/2023

Principal diagnosis: acute pulmonary embolism (right lower lobe segmental), provoked — five days after right knee arthroscopy (10/24/2023).

Course: Heart rate settled over the first night on enoxaparin. Oxygen not required. She walked the halls without symptoms on day two. Nightly TPN continued through her tunneled line. Taught to self-inject enoxaparin; first doses supervised by nursing.

Medication changes:
- START enoxaparin 60 mg subcutaneously every 12 hours, planned 3 months (provoked event).
- STOP norethindrone acetate/ethinyl estradiol (estrogen-containing contraceptive) — not to be restarted. Non-hormonal contraception discussed.
Continue: sertraline 100 mg daily, bupropion XL 150 mg daily, alprazolam 0.25 mg prn, diphenhydramine 25 mg qhs prn, lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, multivitamin, TPN nightly; vedolizumab every 8 weeks with GI.
Stopping estrogen can raise lamotrigine levels; her neurologist has been notified.
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Strongly advised to stop smoking.

documents.title: Prior authorization — enoxaparin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy notified us MassHealth needs prior auth for enoxaparin 60 mg syringes q12h beyond the hospital's discharge supply. PA submitted with dx acute PE and short bowel syndrome (oral anticoagulant absorption unreliable). Approved same day for 90 days. Pharmacy and patient informed.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u. R knee arthroscopy 10/24 (outside ortho); 10/29 sudden SOB → ED, CTA with R lower lobe segmental PE, no RV strain. Observation 10/29–10/31. ED record and discharge summary reviewed, meds reconciled: enoxaparin 60 mg SC q12h started; combined OCP stopped.

Feels much better. Breathing back to normal walking around the apartment. Injecting enoxaparin herself twice a day without trouble, no bleeding. Knee healing, follow-up with the surgeon next week. Still smoking a few cigarettes a week — "the hospital scared me."
Contraception: off the pill now; she and her partner will use condoms. Not interested in an IUD.

Exam: vitals reviewed, HR normal today. Lungs clear. R knee portals healed, no calf tenderness. Abdominal injection sites unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Acute PE, provoked — enoxaparin 60 mg q12h, plan 3 months (through late January), then stop. PA approved. Bleeding precautions reviewed.
2. OCP stopped — estrogen off for good. Barrier method. Neurology to recheck her lamotrigine level now that the estrogen is off; no dizziness or double vision so far.
3. Tobacco — strongly advised to quit; she wants to try cutting down again.
4. s/p R knee arthroscopy — per surgeon.
RTC late January to stop anticoagulation.

NEUROLOGY — RETURN VISIT
Date of service: 03/14/2022

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Bianchi is seen for her yearly review of left temporal lobe epilepsy. She has had no seizures since the single event in December 2020. She takes lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily and has missed very few doses; no rash, dizziness or double vision. Since last year she was treated for a right superior gluteal nerve palsy with physical therapy.

Examination: neurologic examination normal apart from a mild right Trendelenburg gait.

Impression: left temporal lobe epilepsy, well controlled.

Plan: continue lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily; refills from our office. Follow up in one year.

Sincerely,
Neurology

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY — RETURN VISIT
Date of service: 12/04/2023

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Bianchi is seen for her yearly epilepsy review, timed after the hospital let us know of her pulmonary embolism in October and that her estrogen-containing contraceptive was stopped on 10/29. Estrogen lowers lamotrigine levels, so we expected her level to rise off it.

She has had no seizures since December 2020. She remains on lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, now alongside enoxaparin. She reports no dizziness, double vision, unsteadiness or nausea.

Examination: no nystagmus, no ataxia; mild right Trendelenburg gait as before.

Lamotrigine trough today: 8.1 mcg/mL (4.8 on the same dose in 2021; reference 2.5-15.0).

Impression: left temporal lobe epilepsy, well controlled; higher lamotrigine level after the estrogen stop, still in range and without toxicity.

Plan: continue lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, no dose change. She knows to call for dizziness or double vision. Follow up in one year.

Sincerely,
Neurology
